backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/mod.rs:1009-1013 — refresh-token rotation is non-atomic. revoke_token error is only logged ('Continue anyway - better to issue new token than fail') and the handler then issues a NEW refresh token at lines 1035-1063. If revoke fails, the OLD refresh token remains valid alongside the new one — two concurrently valid refresh tokens defeat rotation-based replay detection.
Fix: make revoke+issue atomic in one tx, or fail refresh (500) when revoke fails. (Security property rotation is supposed to provide.)

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/webhook/payment.rs:177-181 — Stripe settlement webhook silently drops a paid event when the invoice is missing. get_invoice returning Ok(None) logs 'Webhook session references a missing invoice' and acks 200 OK → Stripe stops retrying. No metric/alert/dead-letter → a confirmed payment with no matching invoice (race/deletion/drift) is lost.
Fix: before acking, enqueue to a dead-letter/reconciliation path so ops can recover. Keep 200 to avoid retry storms but do not let the event vanish.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/password_reset.rs:62-70 — issuance ignores invalidate_user_tokens result ('let _ = ...'); then stores a fresh reset token at lines 68-84. If invalidate fails, prior unexpired reset tokens remain valid alongside the new one — widens any account-takeover window if an earlier token leaked. The subsequent create error IS handled (line 81), so the silent discard is inconsistent.
Fix: handle invalidate error (log + abort issuance, or invalidate+create in one tx). auth/registration.rs:368 has the same pattern for email-verification tokens (lower value, same fix).
